question: Which of the following statements regarding hydrogen halides HF, HCL, HBr, HI is correct ?:

options.opa: In aqueous solution they have an acid character and their acid strength increases according to HF <HCI <HBr <HI.
options.opb: In all of them there are intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
options.opc: They are all liquid under normal pressure and temperature conditions.
options.opd: They are obtained by oxidation of the corresponding halogen.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: HCl -> dissociates in aqueous solution -> releases H+ ions -> exhibits an acid character -> 90%
CHAIN: HF -> weaker acid compared to HCl, HBr, HI -> acid strength increases in the order HF < HCl < HBr < HI -> 90%
CHAIN: Hydrogen halides -> form intermolecular hydrogen bonds -> due to the presence of hydrogen atoms bonded to electronegative halogen atoms -> 80%
CHAIN: HF -> forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds -> due to the high electronegativity of fluorine -> 80%
CHAIN: HF, HCl, HBr, HI -> gaseous at room temperature -> not liquid under normal pressure and temperature conditions -> 90%
CHAIN: Hydrogen halides -> obtained by the reaction of hydrogen with the corresponding halogen -> not by oxidation -> 90%
analysis: Hydrogen halides HF, HCL, HBr, HI are all acidic in nature, with their acid strength increasing in the order HI > HBr > HCl > HF. They do not form intermolecular hydrogen bonds. They are gases under normal pressure and temperature conditions, except for HF which is a liquid. They are not obtained by oxidation of the corresponding halogen.
